title: Variadic Functions
summary: Functions that take any number of arguments - how printf does it, va_list, va_start, va_arg and va_end, telling the function how many arguments came (a count, a sentinel or a format), default argument promotions, va_copy, wrapping vsnprintf, and letting the compiler check format strings.

cards.q: Why can a variadic function not find out how many arguments it received?
cards.a:
C passes no count or type information, so it must be told by a count, a sentinel or a format

Nothing is passed besides the values themselves. `printf` knows how many to read from its format string; other functions take a count or stop at a sentinel such as NULL.

cards.q: What type should `va_arg` use for an argument that was passed as a `float`?
cards.a:
`double`, because floats are promoted to double when passed through `...`

Default argument promotions turn a float into a double, and char and short into int. Reading it with `va_arg(ap, float)` is undefined behaviour.

cards.q: You need to walk the same va_list twice. What do you use?
cards.a:
va_copy to make a second list

va_copy makes an independent copy that can be walked separately; each needs its own va_end.
